summary: Tested FIX 1 (scroll-to-top on step change) and FEATURE 2 (AI Assess All button) on /prr/{id} Step 7 via Expo web preview at 390x844. FIX 1 PASSES — scrollRef.current?.scrollTo({y:0}) fires on every currentStep change; verified scrollY=0 after navigating Step 2 → 5 → 7 → 2 → 5 → 7 and the 'Step 6-7: Assess & Calculate' title is anchored near the top of the scroll area (bbox.y≈224 after fixed chrome). FEATURE 2 button RENDER PASSES — testID 'ai-assess-all' is visible inside the Assessment Legend card, primary-colored, with the sparkles glyph and 'AI Assess All' label, and the hint line 'Auto-rates every empty cell with AI. Uses AI credits • skips cells missing Expected/Actual values.' is shown directly below. FEATURE 2 CONFIRM + RUN FAILS on web — tapping the button produces no visible dialog/modal, no window.alert/window.confirm event, no POST /api/decisions/{id}/factors/{factorId}/ai-assess request is made, and no progress text appears. Root cause: handleAIAssessAll uses raw react-native Alert.alert(...) with a multi-button Cancel/Assess array; on react-native-web the multi-button Alert.alert is unsupported and silently no-ops. The file already imports the cross-platform showAlert helper (used for XLS/GSheet flows) — those work, so the fix is a one-call-site swap. Same issue affects the post-run 'Out of AI credits' and 'AI Assess All complete' alerts and the 'Nothing to assess'/'All set' guard alerts (all use Alert.alert). Test user wallet balance is -7.89 credits, so even when fixed every cell would 402; the 'Out of AI credits' path is the expected backend outcome but cannot be visually confirmed on web until the Alert.alert calls are migrated to showAlert.

ui_bugs.issue: Multi-button Alert.alert calls render NOTHING on react-native-web, so the entire AI-Assess-All flow is silent on the Expo web preview. Tapping testID 'ai-assess-all' triggers no confirm modal, no /ai-assess POSTs, no progress text, no summary. Affected calls: line 484 'AI Assess All complete', 499 'Nothing to assess', 503 'All set', 506 'AI Assess All' confirm (Cancel/Assess), 475 'Out of AI credits'. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/steps/Step7.tsx:475-514. Fix: replace Alert.alert(...) with showAlert(...) (already imported on line 17 and used by XLS/GSheet flows in the same file).

react_native_issues.issue: Mix of raw react-native Alert.alert and project's showAlert helper in the same file. The file already imports showAlert (line 17) and uses it for XLS/GSheet alerts; the AI/Store alerts (lines 180-248, 353-408, 475-513) still use Alert.alert. On Expo web this means alerts inside those flows are no-ops for multi-button or fall back to ugly window.alert/confirm for single-button. Recommend converting all Alert.alert calls in Step7.tsx to showAlert for consistent web/native UX.

rca_of_issue: FEATURE 2 fails on web because Step7.tsx:506 invokes react-native's Alert.alert with a [Cancel, Assess] multi-button array. react-native-web's Alert polyfill only handles 0-1 button alerts (and even then via ugly window.alert); multi-button alerts are silently dropped, so the user never sees the confirm prompt and runBulkAssess is never invoked. The repository already provides a cross-platform showAlert helper in /app/frontend/src/utils/alert.ts that emits to an AlertHost modal on web, and Step7.tsx already imports and uses it for the XLS/GSheet handlers. Fix is mechanical: swap Alert.alert → showAlert in handleAIAssessAll, runBulkAssess and (recommended) the other AI/Store alert sites in the same file. FIX 1 (scroll reset) is fully working — no further action needed.
